title: Israel's Continuing Rebellion

questions.question: In the seventh year, some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the Lord. What was the Lord's response?",
options: "As I live, declares the Lord God, I will not be inquired of by you."
"Ask, and it shall be given you."
"Why do you inquire of me, seeing you have idols in your heart?"
"I will answer you according to your faith."
questions.correctAnswer: "As I live, declares the Lord God, I will not be inquired of by you."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:3 (ESV): "Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and say to them, Thus says the Lord God, Is it to inquire of me that you come? As I live, declares the Lord God, I will not be inquired of by you."

questions.question: What does God tell Ezekiel to make known to them?
options: The abominations of their fathers
The coming destruction of Babylon
The time of their restoration
The secret sins of their hearts
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:4 (ESV): "Will you judge them, son of man, will you judge them? Let them know the abominations of their fathers,"

questions.question: When God chose Israel and made Himself known to them in Egypt, what did He command them to cast away?
options: The detestable things their eyes feast on, and not defile themselves with the idols of Egypt
The garments of their slavery
Their desire to build cities for Pharaoh
Their foreign wives
questions.correctAnswer: The detestable things their eyes feast on, and not defile themselves with the idols of Egypt
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:7 (ESV): "And I said to them, 'Cast away the detestable things your eyes feast on, every one of you, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.'"

questions.question: Did the people obey God and cast away the idols of Egypt?
options: No, they rebelled against Him and were not willing to listen; they did not cast away the detestable things
Yes, they destroyed all their idols before crossing the Red Sea
Some did, but the tribe of Dan did not
They obeyed initially, but kept a few idols hidden
questions.correctAnswer: No, they rebelled against Him and were not willing to listen; they did not cast away the detestable things
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:8 (ESV): "But they rebelled against me and were not willing to listen to me. None of them cast away the detestable things their eyes feasted on, nor did they forsake the idols of Egypt."

questions.question: Why did God not pour out His wrath on them in Egypt?
options: "But I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations"
"Because I loved Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob"
"Because Moses pleaded with me"
"Because the blood of the lamb was on their doors"
questions.correctAnswer: "But I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:9 (ESV): "But I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they lived,"

questions.question: After bringing them into the wilderness, what did God give them?
options: His statutes and His rules, by which, if a person does them, he shall live
A new king to rule over them
Swords and spears to conquer the land
Manna and quail in abundance
questions.correctAnswer: His statutes and His rules, by which, if a person does them, he shall live
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:11 (ESV): "I gave them my statutes and made known to them my rules, by which, if a person does them, he shall live."

questions.question: What did God give them to be a sign between Him and them, that they might know He is the Lord who sanctifies them?
options: His Sabbaths
The rainbow
Circumcision
The Ark of the Covenant
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:12 (ESV): "Moreover, I gave them my Sabbaths, as a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them."

questions.question: How did the house of Israel treat God's Sabbaths in the wilderness?
options: They greatly profaned them
They kept them joyfully
They ignored them occasionally
They added extra rules to them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:13 (ESV): "But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness... and my Sabbaths they greatly profaned."

questions.question: God swore that He would not bring that generation into the land flowing with milk and honey. But why did His eye spare them from complete destruction in the wilderness?
options: He acted for the sake of His name
Moses stood in the breach
They repented weeping
Their children were innocent
questions.correctAnswer: He acted for the sake of His name
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:14 (ESV): "But I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations, in whose sight I had brought them out." (And 20:17: "Nevertheless, my eye spared them...")

questions.question: What did God say to the children of that generation in the wilderness?
options: "Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor keep their rules, nor defile yourselves with their idols."
"Honor your fathers and mothers no matter what they did."
"Go back to Egypt if you wish."
"You are cursed because of your fathers' sins."
questions.correctAnswer: "Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor keep their rules, nor defile yourselves with their idols."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:18 (ESV): "And I said to their children in the wilderness, 'Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor keep their rules, nor defile yourselves with their idols.'"

questions.question: Did the children obey?
options: No, the children also rebelled against God
Yes, they wholeheartedly followed the Lord
They obeyed but grumbled
They only obeyed after being bitten by snakes
questions.correctAnswer: No, the children also rebelled against God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:21 (ESV): "But the children rebelled against me. They did not walk in my statutes..."

questions.question: When the children repelled, what did God swear He would do to them eventually?
options: Scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries
Turn them into pillars of salt
Send fire from heaven to devour them
Give them a wicked king
questions.correctAnswer: Scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:23 (ESV): "Moreover, I swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries,"

questions.question: Because they had not obeyed His rules, God says He gave them statutes that were not good and rules by which they could not have life. What is an example given?
options: The sacrifice of all their firstborn
The command to eat unclean meat
The law of paying tribute to Babylon
The command to worship the golden calf
questions.correctAnswer: The sacrifice of all their firstborn
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:25-26 (ESV): "Moreover, I gave them statutes that were not good and rules by which they could not have life, and I defiled them through their very gifts in their offering up all their firstborn..."

questions.question: What does God say about the high place they go to, calling it "Bamah" (High Place)?
options: "What is the high place to which you go? So its name is called Bamah to this day."
"It shall be torn down tonight."
"It is a holy place of your fathers."
"Let it be a reminder of your sin."
questions.correctAnswer: "What is the high place to which you go? So its name is called Bamah to this day."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:29 (ESV): "I said to them, What is the high place to which you go? So its name is called Bamah to this day."

questions.question: Despite their rebellion, what does God promise to do with them in the future?
options: "I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you out of the countries where you are scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and with wrath poured out."
"I will forget you forever in Babylon."
"I will let you establish a new nation in Egypt."
"I will send another Moses to divide the river Euphrates."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you out of the countries where you are scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and with wrath poured out."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:34 (ESV): "I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you out of the countries where you are scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and with wrath poured out."

key_verse_text: "Moreover, I gave them my Sabbaths, as a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them."
